Let's start by interpreting our model:

- The model shows $\color{blue}2$ wholes. Each whole is split into *thirds*.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144297/assets/d9c692ed44d98c47b475dc18c2d28a01d0ab1f2f231ed24a9604f14000f599b1.png)

 

- The thirds are grouped, and each group contains ${\color{red}{\dfrac23}}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144297/assets/3c9fd6222f68deffa02ce69a2f31dca220ce2285f71dbd8255d364126ea0d8c8.png)

 

- There are $\color{purple} 3$ groups in total.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144297/assets/228c9e5eea2b5696d64d4423ecd927e12a11e6672d614cc30a947549943be0c4.png)

 

So, if we divide $\color{blue}2$ wholes into groups of ${\color{red}{\dfrac23}},$ we get ${\color{purple}{3}}$ groups in total.

Therefore, the model represents the following division problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144297/assets/bbddce85652f52a2cb4bc4e7c79ccf98a91c2c0953dd8785440c4f9c2515e005.svg)

Therefore, the missing numbers are $\bbox[3pt, Gainsboro]{\color{blue}2}$ and $\bbox[3pt, Gainsboro]{\color{purple}3}.$
